capabilities.why: Before running the untrusted LLM-generated pandas analysis script (Step 7), the agent takes a Celesto snapshot of the clean, configured sandbox. If Step 7 fails (the designed crash point), the system rolls back to this snapshot instead of starting from scratch, saving the cost of reinstalling pandas and re-uploading data. This trades a small snapshot overhead for significant recovery speed and reproducibility.

After the setup phase (pandas install), outbound internet access is disabled inside the sandbox via Celesto network policy. This is the primary defence against prompt-injection exfiltration: even if a poisoned CSV instructs the agent to curl an attacker-controlled endpoint with the LLM_API_KEY, the network-off policy ensures the packet never leaves the microVM guest. The containment test validates this defence end-to-end with a real poisoned CSV.

A pre-command Python callback (safety_hook) runs on the host before every command is forwarded to the guest sandbox. It inspects the command string against a blocklist of destructive patterns (rm -rf /, dd if=/dev/zero) and exfiltration signatures (curl.*API_KEY). Blocked commands are still appended to the audit log with decision=block. This provides a host-level, code-enforced guardrail that is completely separate from the LLM system prompt and cannot be bypassed by prompt injection alone.
